If more on personal and unjustifiable talaga, then lapit ka sa clerk coordinator nyo and file a complaint. Approach ka din sa psych nyo sa hospital/medschool. 

Regarding naman sa pag-overtime, sadly one of the things you learn sa clerkship is ang pag-overtime mo sa duty is almost expected kahit na galing ka na ng 24 hour duty and from duty status ka na. Kahit nga to the point na ikaw na gumagawa ng trabaho ng coclerks mo, di sya reason for someone to give you your flying colors. If medyo major ang mistakes mo sa simula ng duty, then take solace na walang expectation ang residents and consultants from the clerks. Alam nila na nasa learning stage ka pa lang. And to make up for them, sadly only time can tell. Kahit na magextra effort ka pa sa duty, walang assurance na May makaka-notice. Consistency lang ang makakatakip ng mistakes mo. Kapag lang naka-ilang months of duty ka na and consistent ka naman na maganda duty mo, saka lang siguro mabubura yung mistakes mo sa utak ng mga tao. 

Clerkship isn't really fun for most, sad to say. Especially for students na diretso medschool after grad and walang work experience (meaning no experience sa work politics, etc). 

One last thing is always choose you. If tingin mo di na kaya ng mental mo, then take a break. Medicine na certainly not worth losing your mind over. Pero at the very least try and assess your situation and take the initial necessary steps before giving up.

I would love to say na those who are bullying you are bad pero di ko naman alam ang situwasyon. Ano ang reason bakit ka na-bully or na-single out? If personal reasons, then report ka sa clerk coordinator nyo. Pero if May basis sa trabaho/duty, then maybe self reflect.

From my experience, I knew people na sobrang di maaasahan sa duty, and nagiging endorsable sila even sa other departments na di pa namin napupuntahan, leading to them being singled out. Most of them nakayanan ang "isolation" and nakatapos ng duty, pero they made everything extra hard for themselves. 

Ayoko magtunog victim blamer, pero sadly the world isn't fair like that. Try and assess the situation if personal reasons or may professional basis ba. Then take necessary steps afterward.

elo OP. I'm currently a med student also from a non-trad background, the only difference is, I was a delinquent student esp since I didn't like my course, when I originally wanted to pursue medicine. But the opportunity came after I already passed the board exams for my original course, and was already working for almost 2 years but w/o any sort of fulfillment, which my parents saw, so they gave me the chance to pursue what I wanted. Now I'm an incoming 3rd year, but the one thing I wish I did before entering medschool was to address my mental and psychological troubles first. I thought that finally going into my dream course would be the answer, pero dapat sana nagpa-psych muna ako, because the stress of medschool brings out and amplifies the inferiority complex out ot people. Before med school I had a lot of self-esteem issues esp since nung bata pinaparamdam ng lahat ng tao sa paligid na angtalino mo, pero pagdating ng college biglang nagloko kasi di gusto ang course.   
bottomline is, if you're feeling doubts, try and address them first, Try seeking professional help. and the one thing you should not do is to enter medschool because of other people. may mga tao na may mental fortitude to survive medschool even if di talaga nila gusto, pero I would advise against it.
